topic.title: Preference Alignment Objectives and Noisy Feedback
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Preference alignment adjusts language models using comparisons, rewards, or related supervision. The topic focuses on the mathematical objective: calibration, divergence choice, noise correction, and how ties or biased comparisons affect learning. A preference label is a measurement with uncertainty, not necessarily a clean statement of one universal utility.
topic.whyItMatters: Poorly modeled feedback can reward spurious distinctions or amplify annotation errors. Direct alignment objectives offer simpler training than online reinforcement learning, but their statistical meaning still depends on the assumed feedback process.
topic.evolution: A 2016 representative connects task rewards with maximum-likelihood learning for structured outputs. More recent work develops direct preference optimization, explicit-reward alignment, and calibrated losses. The newest papers examine noise tolerance, representation-distance bias, and self-consuming data loops. This progression highlights feedback quality and objective design alongside computational simplicity.
openQuestions: Which preference-noise assumptions can be checked from real annotation data?
How should ties and legitimate disagreement influence alignment rather than be discarded?

papers.title: DeepHalo: A Neural Choice Model with Controllable Context Effects

papers.title: Direct Alignment with Heterogeneous Preferences
papers.tldr: Accounting for differing user preferences improves direct alignment, but the paper establishes a tension between consistent learning and sample efficiency.

papers.title: Distortion of AI Alignment: Does Preference Optimization Optimize for Preferences?
papers.tldr: A social-choice analysis shows that preference-alignment methods can differ sharply in their worst-case protection of average user utility.

papers.title: Distributional LLM-as-a-Judge
papers.tldr: Training LLM judges to match distributions of human judgments improves reported alignment and robustness while retaining competitive accuracy.

papers.title: Distributive Fairness in Large Language Models: Evaluating Alignment with Human Values
papers.tldr: Evaluated language models diverge from human distributional preferences, with some responding markedly differently when selecting allocations instead of generating them.

papers.title: Doubly Robust Alignment for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Doubly robust preference optimization remains consistent when either its preference model or its reference policy is correctly specified.

papers.title: Elastic Robust Unlearning of Specific Knowledge in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: ERU combines flexible rewards with refusal feature ablation to improve targeted unlearning and its robustness to tested retraining attacks.

papers.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback to Improve Alignment
papers.tldr: The paper links unwanted RLHF responses to selected training examples and unlearns those examples to improve some responses while largely preserving satisfactory behavior.

papers.title: Generative RLHF-V: Learning Principles from Multi-modal Human Preference
papers.tldr: Generative RLHF-V combines reasoning-based preference judgments with grouped response comparisons to improve multimodal reinforcement learning from human feedback.

papers.title: Greedy Sampling Is Provably Efficient For RLHF
papers.tldr: Greedy preference sampling receives stronger RLHF guarantees by exploiting KL-regularized policy structure.

papers.title: GVPO: Group Variance Policy Optimization for Large Language Model Post-Training
papers.tldr: GVPO derives language-model post-training updates from KL-constrained reward maximization, with a unique optimum and flexible sampling distributions.

papers.title: HelpSteer3-Preference: Open Human-Annotated Preference Data across Diverse Tasks and Languages
papers.tldr: HelpSteer3-Preference releases over 40,000 human preference samples and supports reward models with strong reported benchmark performance.

papers.title: Implicit Reward as the Bridge: A Unified View of SFT and DPO Connections
papers.tldr: A shared implicit-reward framework connects SFT and DPO and motivates learning-rate and objective changes that improve post-training performance.

papers.title: Improving LLM General Preference Alignment via Optimistic Online Mirror Descent
papers.tldr: A game-based alignment method handles general preferences and improves both theoretical convergence rates and reported benchmark performance.

papers.title: Inference-time Alignment in Continuous Space
papers.tldr: SEA aligns responses at inference time by refining continuous latent representations with gradient-based sampling.

papers.title: Inference-Time Personalized Alignment with a Few User Preference Queries
papers.tldr: UserAlign selects personalized responses from a fixed candidate pool using a few pairwise comparisons under consistent, noise-free feedback.

papers.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes inference-time reward hacking and introduces HedgeTune to moderate proxy optimization and improve reward-distortion tradeoffs.

papers.title: InfiFPO: Implicit Model Fusion via Preference Optimization in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: InfiFPO fuses source-model sequence probabilities within preference optimization, improving a pivot model across eleven evaluated benchmarks.

papers.title: KL Penalty Control via Perturbation for Direct Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: Epsilon-DPO adapts reference-model regularization for each preference pair using changes in preference confidence under penalty perturbations.

papers.title: KL-Regularized RLHF with Multiple Reference Models: Exact Solutions and Sample Complexity
papers.tldr: The paper gives an exact multiple-reference solution for reverse-KL RLHF and analyzes sample complexity for both KL directions.

papers.title: Less is More: Improving LLM Alignment via Preference Data Selection
papers.tldr: Margin-based preference selection and Bayesian aggregation improve evaluated DPO models while using substantially smaller training subsets.

papers.title: Leveraging robust optimization for llm alignment under distribution shifts
papers.tldr: Classifier-calibrated robust optimization focuses preference training on the human-preferred distribution to mitigate synthetic-data mismatch.

papers.title: Limited Preference Data? Learning Better Reward Model with Latent Space Synthesis
papers.tldr: LENS synthesizes preference pairs in embedding space to improve reward modeling while greatly reducing reported generation cost.

papers.title: Majority of the Bests: Improving Best-of-N via Bootstrapping
papers.tldr: Majority-of-the-Bests bootstraps Best-of-N selections and chooses their most frequent answer, improving results in 25 of 30 tested setups.

papers.title: Meta-Learning Objectives for Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: The paper searches for preference-optimization objectives in cheaper MuJoCo tasks and transfers the resulting insights to improve an LLM alignment task.

papers.title: Mitigating Reward Over-optimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms with Importance Sampling
papers.tldr: Clipped importance weighting helps direct alignment methods reduce distribution shift and the performance degradation caused by over-optimization.

papers.title: On Extending Direct Preference Optimization to Accommodate Ties
papers.tldr: Two tie-aware DPO variants make equal-preference comparisons usable and show benefits for regularization and several evaluated tasks.

papers.title: Pairwise Calibrated Rewards for Pluralistic Alignment
papers.tldr: Pairwise-calibrated reward ensembles preserve preference disagreement by matching how often annotators favor each response.

papers.title: Pre-Trained Policy Discriminators are General Reward Models
papers.tldr: POLAR pretrains reward models to distinguish policies, improving preference judgments and reward-guided language-model training.

papers.title: Preference-based Reinforcement Learning beyond Pairwise Comparisons: Benefits of Multiple Options
papers.tldr: Under a Plackett–Luce ranking model, M-AUPO provides guarantees that explicitly improve as feedback ranks larger action subsets.

papers.title: Preference Distillation via Value based Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: TVKD improves preference training with teacher-value rewards designed to preserve DPO's optimal policy without requiring additional rollouts.

papers.title: Preference Optimization by Estimating the Ratio of the Data Distribution
papers.tldr: BPO generalizes DPO through likelihood-ratio matching, with target-policy guarantees and reported improvements in both win rate and entropy.

papers.title: Proximalized Preference Optimization for Diverse Feedback Types: A Decomposed Perspective on DPO
papers.tldr: PRO restores an overlooked regularization component in preference optimization to resolve likelihood underdetermination and support diverse feedback.

papers.title: Quantile Reward Policy Optimization: Alignment with Pointwise Regression and Exact Partition Functions
papers.tldr: QRPO uses quantile rewards and an exact normalization term to enable offline alignment from individual response rewards.

papers.title: Rectifying Shortcut Behaviors in Preference-based Reward Learning
papers.tldr: PRISM uses invariant reward representations to reduce reliance on spurious preference cues and improve out-of-distribution reward accuracy.

papers.title: Reducing the Probability of Undesirable Outputs in Language Models Using Probabilistic Inference
papers.tldr: RePULSe targets sampled low-reward responses during training, improving the tradeoff between average reward and undesirable-output probability.

papers.title: RePO: Understanding Preference Learning Through ReLU-Based Optimization
papers.tldr: RePO achieves competitive preference learning with a simple ReLU objective whose threshold filters examples to help prevent over-optimization.

papers.title: ResponseRank: Data-Efficient Reward Modeling through Preference Strength Learning
papers.tldr: ResponseRank learns preference strength from locally comparable noisy signals, improving sample efficiency and robustness in the reported tasks.

papers.title: Reverse Engineering Human Preferences with Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Reinforcement-trained preamble generators raise LLM-judge scores for frozen models and transfer to unseen candidate–judge pairings.

papers.title: Risk-aware Direct Preference Optimization under Nested Risk Measure
papers.tldr: Ra-DPO incorporates nested risk measures and token-level deviation control to better balance preference alignment with reference-model drift.

papers.title: Robust LLM Alignment via Distributionally Robust Direct Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: Two distributionally robust DPO methods improve reported alignment under shifts between training and deployment preferences.

papers.title: Scalable Valuation of Human Feedback through Provably Robust Model Alignment
papers.tldr: Hölder-DPO combines provably robust preference alignment with a scalable metric for detecting and valuing noisy human feedback.

papers.title: Sparta Alignment: Collectively Aligning Multiple Language Models through Combat
papers.tldr: Sparta Alignment improves multiple language models through peer-judged competitions that generate shared preference-training data.

papers.title: Stackelberg Self-Annotation: A Robust Approach to Data-Efficient LLM Alignment
papers.tldr: A robust game-based alignment framework expands a small human preference seed through self-annotation while controlling annotation-noise sensitivity.

papers.title: Teaching Language Models to Evolve with Users: Dynamic Profile Modeling for Personalized Alignment
papers.tldr: RLPA trains language models to update user profiles through dialogue, improving personalized responses in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: Token-Level Self-Play with Importance-Aware Guidance for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: SWIFT uses a stronger teacher to weight individual tokens during self-play, improving both alignment and knowledge distillation in reported experiments.

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware Preference Alignment for Diffusion Policies
papers.tldr: Diff-UAPA directly tunes diffusion policies to diverse human preferences using a Bayesian objective that mitigates inconsistent feedback.

papers.title: VPO: Reasoning Preferences Optimization Based on $\mathcal{V}$-Usable Information
papers.tldr: VPO selectively limits negative preference-training gradients to reduce harmful probability shifts and improve mathematical reasoning performance.

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization under Distribution Shifts
papers.tldr: RAVEN learns which weak supervisors to trust when training a stronger model across distribution shifts.

papers.title: What Makes a Reward Model a Good Teacher? An Optimization Perspective
papers.tldr: Reward-model accuracy alone does not ensure effective RLHF: low induced reward variance can make optimization extremely slow, even with perfect accuracy.

papers.title: What Matters in Data for DPO?
papers.tldr: Theory and experiments identify chosen-response quality as the dominant driver of DPO performance, with rejected-response quality potentially less influential.

papers.title: ActiveUltraFeedback: Efficient Preference Data Generation using Active Learning
papers.tldr: ActiveUltraFeedback selects informative preference comparisons, achieving comparable or better downstream results with as little as one-sixth of the annotated data.

papers.title: Alignment-Aware Decoding
papers.tldr: Alignment-aware decoding improves preference alignment during generation and can supply synthetic data that improves alignment under standard decoding.

papers.title: Alignment Tampering: How Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback Is Exploited to Optimize Misaligned Biases
papers.tldr: Alignment tampering can make preference-based training amplify unwanted biases when those biases accompany higher-quality answers.

papers.title: Asymptotic Universal Alignment: A New Alignment Framework via Test-Time Scaling
papers.tldr: A theoretical alignment framework shows how diverse candidate responses can achieve an optimal improvement in user-preference win rates as sampling increases.

papers.title: Autoregressive Direct Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: ADPO derives preference optimization with autoregressive modeling built in from the start and distinguishes token length from feedback length.

papers.title: CAMEL: Confidence-Gated Reflection for Reward Modeling
papers.tldr: CAMEL improves preference judging by making quick initial decisions and reserving trained self-correction for low-confidence cases.

papers.title: Conditional Equivalence of DPO and RLHF: Implicit Assumption, Failure Modes, and Provable Alignment
papers.tldr: DPO's equivalence to RLHF depends on a preference-ordering assumption, motivating a constrained method with provable alignment.

papers.title: Conflict-Aware Adaptive Alignment for LLM Hallucination Mitigation
papers.tldr: CAMP adapts preference training to samples where truthfulness and helpfulness conflict, improving truthfulness with a favorable helpfulness trade-off.

papers.title: Consistency Training Can Entrench Misalignment
papers.tldr: Consistency training has behavior-dependent alignment effects, generally reducing some misalignment while amplifying sycophancy in controlled experiments.

papers.title: Convex Optimization for Alignment and Preference Learning on a Single GPU
papers.tldr: COALA applies convex optimization to preference fine-tuning, enabling single-GPU training with competitive performance and substantially reduced computation.

papers.title: DARC: Disagreement-Aware Alignment via Risk-Constrained Decoding
papers.tldr: DARC reranks responses using disagreement-aware risk controls, reducing tail risk while maintaining competitive average quality without retraining.

papers.title: Discovering Implicit Large Language Model Alignment Objectives
papers.tldr: Obj-Disco translates alignment rewards into sparse natural-language objectives and can expose unintended incentives alongside desired behaviors.

papers.title: Distortion of AI Alignment Revisited: RLHF is a Decent Utilitarian Aligner
papers.tldr: An analysis of RLHF with reward clipping links severe average-utility distortion to distribution mismatch and shows optimal distortion proportional to beta when the distributions match.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.tldr: Distributionally robust versions of RLHF and DPO improve tested performance when deployment tasks differ from the preference-training data.

papers.title: DPO Unchained: Your Training Algorithm is Secretly Disentangled in Human Choice Theory (and Its Loss’ Convexity is Dispensable)
papers.tldr: The paper broadens DPO’s choice-theoretic foundations to support independently combined modeling choices, non-convex losses, and common extensions.

papers.title: Efficient Preference Poisoning Attack on Offline RLHF
papers.tldr: For log-linear DPO, preference-label poisoning becomes a structured binary selection problem with conditional recovery and robustness guarantees.

papers.title: Federated Variational Preference Alignment with Gumbel-Softmax Prior for Personalized User Preferences
papers.tldr: FedVPA-GP uses a shared population prior and separated preference prototypes to improve personalized federated alignment and support preference switching.

papers.title: GenAlign: Towards Unified Alignment Framework of MLLMs via Generative Reward Model
papers.tldr: GenAlign combines a rubric-guided, position-debiased reward model with efficient policy optimization to improve multimodal alignment.

papers.title: How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy
papers.tldr: The paper explains how preference-induced reward gaps can amplify sycophancy and derives a minimal agreement penalty to prevent that increase.

papers.title: Implicit Preference Alignment for Human Image Animation
papers.tldr: Implicit Preference Alignment improves animated hands using self-generated quality samples and local optimization without paired preference data.

papers.title: Inference-Aware Meta-Alignment of LLMs via Non-Linear GRPO
papers.tldr: IAMA trains language models for efficient inference-time alignment and introduces non-linear GRPO with an optimality guarantee in probability-measure space.

papers.title: Inference-time Alignment with Rewards in Besov Spaces: Provable Advantages of Feature Learning and Multi-Step Policy Updates
papers.tldr: Under a Besov-space reward assumption, feature learning and repeated reward-model refitting provide provable advantages for inference-time alignment.

papers.title: IRPM: Intergroup Relative Preference Modeling for Pointwise Generative Reward Models
papers.tldr: IRPM learns comparable per-response rewards from grouped preference comparisons, enabling linear-cost evaluation of candidate sets.

papers.title: Layer-wise Gradient Disentanglement: Decoupling Semantics and Preferences in Direct Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: GDO-DPO uses layer-specific gradient stability to separately pace learning of prompt semantics and response preferences.

papers.title: Leveraging Machine Unlearning for Cost-Efficient Preference Alignment
papers.tldr: U2A selects and weights negative examples for unlearning according to their estimated effect on preference alignment.

papers.title: Maximizing Mutual Information Between Prompt and Response Improves LLM Performance With No Additional Data
papers.tldr: MIPO improves tested language models using preference pairs generated from matching and unrelated prompts, without additional external supervision.

papers.title: Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning
papers.tldr: SA-DPO adapts preference margins to semantic distance, addressing consistency failures identified for standard surrogate losses.

papers.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in LLM-based Recommendation: A Preference Optimization Approach
papers.tldr: SIRIUS uses pseudo-negatives to strengthen weak ranking signals and reduce reward hacking in language-model recommendation.

papers.title: Multi-Objective Preference Optimization: Improving Human Alignment of Generative Models
papers.tldr: MOPO aligns models with multiple preferences by optimizing a primary goal while enforcing tunable minimum levels for secondary goals.

papers.title: Normalized Rewards for Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: Regularizing response probabilities improves evaluated preference-optimization trade-offs and reduces likelihood displacement concentrated in outlier tokens.

papers.title: One Bias After Another: Mechanistic Reward Shaping and Persistent Biases in Language Reward Models
papers.tldr: The paper documents persistent reward-model biases and introduces a lightweight internal intervention that mitigates targeted low-complexity biases.

papers.title: Pareto-Guided Optimal Transport for Multi-Reward Alignment
papers.tldr: PG-OT aligns image generators using prompt-specific Pareto frontiers to balance rewards and mitigate reward hacking.

papers.title: PortraitRL: Reinforcement Learning for Portrait Pose Transfer with Multi-Objective Reward
papers.tldr: PortraitRL uses calibrated visual rewards and automatically derived preferences to improve identity preservation and pose-editing accuracy.

papers.title: Position: RLHF May Not Reflect Genuine Preferences
papers.tldr: Analysis of two RLHF datasets shows that inconsistent annotations can systematically distort the preferences and harm judgments attributed to people.

papers.title: Positive–Unlabeled Reinforcement Learning Distillation for On-Premise Small Models
papers.tldr: One teacher response per prompt anchors local student self-ranking, enabling low-cost preference optimization without human preference labels or a reward model.

papers.title: Probability-Entropy Calibration: An Elastic Indicator for Adaptive Fine-tuning
papers.tldr: RankTuner calibrates token-level fine-tuning weights using the correct token’s rank relative to the model’s predictive distribution.

papers.title: Real-Time Aligned Reward Model beyond Semantics
papers.tldr: R2M uses a policy’s evolving hidden states to help its reward model track distribution shifts during reinforcement learning.

papers.title: REAR: Test-time Preference Realignment through Reward Decomposition
papers.tldr: REAR rebalances question and preference rewards during inference to improve preference alignment without additional model training.

papers.title: Reliability-Aware LLM Alignment from Inconsistent Human Feedback
papers.tldr: RGPO weights preference learning by annotator reliability and consensus to reduce the impact of inconsistent human feedback.

papers.title: Reward-free Alignment for Conflicting Objectives
papers.tldr: RACO uses pairwise preferences and conflict-aware gradient updates to improve multi-objective alignment trade-offs without explicit reward models.

papers.title: Reward Shaping for (Inference-Time) Alignment: A Stackelberg Game Perspective
papers.tldr: A game-theoretic reward-shaping method improves inference-time alignment by accounting for how KL regularization preserves base-policy biases.

papers.title: Robust AI Evaluation through Maximal Lotteries
papers.tldr: Robust lotteries aggregate subjective model comparisons while protecting against plausible shifts in annotator and prompt preferences.

papers.title: RSPO: Regularized Self-Play Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: RSPO adds interchangeable regularizers to self-play alignment, preserving game-equilibrium convergence and improving reported preference and diversity results.

papers.title: Simultaneous Multi-objective Alignment Across Verifiable and Non-verifiable Rewards
papers.tldr: MAHALO coordinates verifiable and subjective alignment objectives while allowing users to adjust objective priorities during inference.

papers.title: Spurious Correlation Learning in Preference Optimization: Mechanisms, Consequences, and Mitigation via Tie Training
papers.tldr: Tie training uses equal-utility preference pairs to reduce spurious feature learning that more data from the same distribution cannot eliminate.

papers.title: T-POP: Test-Time Personalization with Online Preference Feedback
papers.tldr: T-POP personalizes a frozen language model by learning from online user comparisons and steering decoding with the resulting preference reward.

papers.title: Task-Aware Preference Calibration for Direct Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: TAPC calibrates preference-label confidence by task type, improving DPO especially on creative and open-ended tasks.

papers.title: Temporal Self-Rewarding Language Models: Decoupling Chosen-Rejected via Past-Future
papers.tldr: Temporal self-rewarding preserves preference-learning contrast by anchoring rejected answers in an earlier model and selecting preferred answers with later predictions.

papers.title: $\textitS$-SPPO: Semantic-Calibrated Self-Play Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: S-SPPO stabilizes self-play preference learning by reducing overconfident judgments between similar responses and preserving representation diversity.

papers.title: The Differences Between Direct Alignment Algorithms are a Blur
papers.tldr: In a unified comparison of direct alignment methods, ranking objectives matter more for quality than the particular scalar scores being optimized.

papers.title: The Hidden Link between RLHF and Contrastive Learning
papers.tldr: A contrastive-learning interpretation of RLHF and DPO motivates MIO, which mitigates preferred-response likelihood decline and performs competitively on reasoning benchmarks.

papers.title: The Sign Estimator: Preference Modeling for LLM Alignment under Heterogeneity
papers.tldr: Under a stated assumption, the Sign Estimator learns rankings consistent with population-average utility despite heterogeneous human preferences.

papers.title: Threshold-Guided Optimization for Visual Generative Models
papers.tldr: A data-driven score threshold lets visual generators learn preference alignment directly from unpaired scalar feedback.

papers.title: TokenRatio: Principled Token-Level Preference Optimization via Ratio Matching
papers.tldr: TBPO learns token-level preferences from sequence comparisons through ratio matching, improving alignment, stability, and diversity in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Towards Disentangled Preference Optimization Dynamics: Suppress the Loser, Preserve the Winner
papers.tldr: Reward calibration rebalances preference updates to help suppress rejected responses while preserving chosen ones under a testable condition.

papers.title: Transitivity Meets Cyclicity: Explicit Preference Decomposition for Dynamic Large Language Model Alignment
papers.tldr: HRC separates hierarchical and cyclic preferences, while dynamic self-play uses that structure to improve evaluated language-model alignment.

papers.title: Unbiased Alignment for Large Language Models with Noisy Preferences
papers.tldr: URM and UDPO correct preference-noise distortion in alignment losses, enabling theoretically unbiased training without clean ground-truth supervision.

papers.title: Unbiased Reward Modeling from Implicit Feedback for LLM Alignment
papers.tldr: ImplicitRM models hidden feedback groups to address missing negatives and selection bias when learning rewards from user interactions.

papers.title: What Does Preference Learning Recover from Pairwise Comparison Data?
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes when Bradley–Terry fits pairwise preference data and identifies margin and connectivity as drivers of sample efficiency.

papers.title: When and How Human Curation Backfires: Preference Alignment under Multi-Model Self-Consuming Loop
papers.tldr: In interacting synthetic-data training loops, cross-model feedback can weaken or reverse the alignment benefits of human curation.

papers.title: When Distance Distracts: Representation Distance Bias in BT-Loss for Reward Models
papers.tldr: NormBT normalizes preference-learning updates to reduce representation-distance bias and improve reward models’ handling of fine-grained response differences.

papers.title: When Labelers Stay Silent: The Power of Ties in Cost-Effective Preference Learning
papers.tldr: Explicitly modelling ties reduces unreliable preference updates and lets small-model supervision outperform stronger forced-choice labelers in the reported experiments.
